claims.text: A Govee lamp is a culture-rules actor any workflow can drive, and a daily wake-up workflow fades it in at 06:20

honesty_conditions.text: a lamp_* step run from culture-rules changes the real H6076 lamp, seen in govee stats with source rules

claims.text: The lamp is reached through a culture-rules runner actor whose params.commands registry (culture_rules/actors/code.py) holds govee-cli's named lamp commands (lamp_on, lamp_off, lamp_brightness, lamp_color, lamp_temp, lamp_scene, lamp_fade_on, lamp_fade_off), each argv the absolute govee path ending --source rules --apply --json; govee-cli generates the definition with 'govee rules actor' (govee-cli docs/culture-rules/README.md)

honesty_conditions.text: the actor's commands are exactly what 'govee rules actor' prints on spark, every argv[0] absolute and no argv a shell or interpreter, so inline_guard admits all 8

claims.text: No culture-rules code change, no new actor kind, app surface or lamp.* action kind: ACTOR_KINDS already has runner (culture_rules/model/actor.py:15) and a step calls a registered command by name, so the lamp actor is configuration only

honesty_conditions.text: the delivered change touches no file under culture_rules/ or web/; only live store records (actor, workflow, rule) and docs change

claims.text: govee serve runs on spark as an always-on user unit (docs/systemd/govee-serve.service) so a long fade runs inside serve and the runner step returns at once, scenes see GOVEE_API_KEY, and the runner authenticates with a token saved by 'govee token new --name culture-rules --save'

hard_questions.text: Does govee serve become an always-on unit on spark as part of this, or does the runner call the lamp directly over LAN (a long fade then holds the step)?
hard_questions.resolution: govee serve becomes an always-on user unit on spark

claims.text: govee-cli owns the lamp command list and the actor definition; culture-rules commits no govee actor JSON (the argv path is per machine, govee-cli README) and no wake-up bundle; schedules live in culture-rules' store, never in govee-cli

honesty_conditions.text: no govee actor JSON and no wake-up schedule is committed in govee-cli; culture-rules commits at most a disabled example bundle
git diff of the delivery holds no govee actor JSON and no wake-up workflow or rule in either repo; the actor, workflow and rule exist only in the live store

revisions.text: govee-cli owns the lamp command list and the actor definition; culture-rules commits no govee actor JSON (the argv path is per machine, govee-cli README) and schedules live in culture-rules, never in govee-cli

claims.text: The wake-up is a schedule rule (stdlib cron, IANA tz Asia/Jerusalem) at 06:20 daily that starts a workflow whose step calls the lamp actor's fade-in command; the step is placed on the machine the lamp's runner lives on (spark)

honesty_conditions.text: the rule's trigger is kind schedule with cron 20 6 * * * and tz Asia/Jerusalem, and its workflow step is placed on spark where the runner and the lamp's LAN are

claims.text: Wake-up details (target brightness, colour or temperature, fade length, weekdays only, snooze, skip when away) are not in this frame; they are workflow configuration set later
The installed govee on spark (~/.local/bin/govee 0.11.0) is reinstalled from merged govee-cli main before import; today it lacks the rules verb ('invalid choice: rules')
The operator at home on spark, and any culture-rules workflow author who wants a lamp as a step

honesty_conditions.text: the operator, not a mesh agent, enables the wake-up rule; any workflow author can add a lamp step without touching govee-cli

claims.text: The lamp is one enabled actor in the Actors tab; any workflow calls lamp_* commands by name with typed args, and a schedule rule fades the lamp in each morning at 06:20 Asia/Jerusalem

honesty_conditions.text: culture-rules actors references on the lamp actor lists the wake-up workflow, and the actor is enabled on machine spark

claims.text: govee-cli can drive the lamp from its CLI, web console and MCP, but no culture-rules actor exists for it, so no rule or workflow can touch the lamp

honesty_conditions.text: before this delivery no culture-rules actor had a govee argv (checked live with actors list once a token is set)

claims.text: Lights become a reusable output of the mesh (CI red, wake-up, bedtime) by configuration alone, with govee-cli keeping ownership of how the lamp is spoken to

honesty_conditions.text: a second flow can use the lamp with only a new workflow step, no new actor and no code

claims.text: On 1 morning after enabling, the run at 06:20 Asia/Jerusalem succeeds within 60 s of the scheduled time, govee's event log shows the fade with source rules, and the lamp ends on

honesty_conditions.text: the first morning's run record and govee stats (source rules) are read back and attached as evidence, not assumed

scope_entries.finding: govee-cli (PR #3, merged) already ships 'govee rules actor', which prints a runner actor with 8 typed commands; fade commands carry a 3660 s timeout; argv[0] is absolute because runner commands start with PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin only

ACTOR_KINDS = agent, human, service, daemon, runner, robot, app; APP_SURFACES = github, jira, discord, email, search; nothing lamp-specific is needed; the steps-generic memory forbids a flow-specific builtin

scope_entries.surface: govee-cli README 'Run it with govee serve' + systemctl --user is-active govee-serve
scope_entries.finding: govee-serve is inactive on spark today (2026-10-30); without it a 20-minute fade blocks the runner step for its whole length and lamp_scene cannot see the API key

scope_entries.surface: govee-cli README 'Schedules live in culture-rules, not here'
scope_entries.finding: govee-cli has no timers of its own; when a command fires is the rule's business

scope_entries.surface: CLAUDE.md second mile: schedule trigger (stdlib cron, UTC or an IANA tz)
scope_entries.finding: a schedule trigger already exists; the newspaper bundle uses Asia/Jerusalem the same way
installed binary refuses 'rules' even though the repo's 0.11.0 has it; the tool install predates PR #3's last commits
registered commands run shell=False with typed params, in a temp dir, minimal env; supports_idempotency_key=False so an unknown outcome is not re-run unless the step is declared idempotent
